data.hypothesis: On the supplied GH200/CUDA 12.6.3 target, reusing warpReduceSum for warp 0's final aggregation may let the int specialization use __reduce_add_sync instead of the current two shuffle-down additions. Only the CTA-local final combine changes; the 128-thread geometry, one-value-per-lane load, tail identity, stage schedule, scratch selection, and final copy remain fixed. The controller's complete-run timing must establish whether this instruction-level change helps independently of launch topology.

memory_lessons.applicability: This reduction objective and fixed 128-thread geometry.
memory_lessons.claim: The four measured CTA-local candidates were all valid and correct, with four distinct programs. Their complete-run means are close: the best listed CUB default result is about 0.9% faster than the selected warp-centric parent, so small local changes may be difficult to distinguish from complete-run costs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the final-combine-only redux variant against the selected parent without changing the launch or stage schedule.

data.notes: No commands or measurements were run. Prior controller measurements are complete-run results: baseline 46.7866 μs; selected warp-centric parent 29.4874 μs; measured CUB default 29.2154 μs; explicit CUB warp-reductions policy 29.7291 μs. The supplied catalog reports four distinct valid programs. These results do not establish the performance of this unmeasured final-combine variant; the unchanged launch topology makes the controller's comparison the evidence for whether this local change helps.
transformations: Replace the two final shuffle-down additions with a full-warp warpReduceSum call over the four warp totals and zero-valued remaining lanes.
Keep the launch geometry, per-lane input load, tail handling, scratch schedule and final copy unchanged.
